deities: Lord Tryambakeshwara (Shiva) - Swayambhu (self-manifested) Shiva Lingam; darshanam faces the sea
festivals: Annual 7-day festival in Kumbham (February-March) starting on Panchami with kodiyettam; ezhinellippu of Keezhoor Sastha and Kuthirakali thidambu; Ashtami Vilakku; Pallivetta on the last day
Theyyam Kaliyattam on Kumbham 26 (March 10); main theyyam is Moovalamkuzhi Chamundi; Thidambu Nritham
Amavasi (new moon) Pitru Tarpanam - thousands gather for ancestral rites

history.dynasty: Historically associated with Chirakkal Kovilakam; later administered by the Anjuru Achannmar (500 Nair families)
history.period: Consecration (pratishta) attributed to Kanva Maharshi per legend; no documented founding date (verify)
history.summary: A rare seashore Shiva temple on the Arabian Sea coast, popularly 'Dakshina Kashi', and one of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala - one of the rarest shrines in the state dedicated to Tryambakeshwara Shiva. The Swayambhu lingam's consecration is credited to Kanva Maharshi; it is also counted among the 108 Shiva temples established by Parasurama. Legend says the darshanam originally faced east but was turned to face west towards the sea to placate the deity's fierce (ugramurti) form. Unusually, two Tantri families - the Edamana Tantri (Uchillath) and the Olayath Tantri - conduct rituals in alternate years. The Kshetra Thattakam once covered 30 villages. Shiveli is performed thrice daily, unlike most temples. The temple is famous for Amavasi pitru tarpanam and is attended by Bekal, Kottikkulam, Palakunnu and Muchilottu Bhagavathi during the festival. Nearby Pandiyan Kallu (a sea rock ~2 km away) is linked to a legend of a Pandya king's ship turned to stone for attacking the temple. CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is NOT in Kasaragod town - it is at Thrikkannad near Bekal (Kasaragod-Kanhangad road), about 1 km from Bekal and ~12 km from Kasaragod town. Documented with the corrected location.

name: Trikkannad Tryambakeshwara Temple
town: Trikkannad, Bekal (CSV town 'Kasaragod' is the district HQ ~12 km away - corrected)
town_description: Trikkannad is on the Arabian seashore about 1 km from Bekal, on the Kasaragod-Kanhangad road in Kasaragod district. Bekal Fort and Bekal Fort Beach are nearby, making the temple an easy stop on the Bekal sightseeing circuit.

travel.railway: Nearest stations Bekal Fort and Kanhangad (verify).
travel.road: On the Kasaragod-Kanhangad road (via Chandragiri), about 1 km from Bekal; buses/taxis from Kasaragod and Kanhangad.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Kumbham (February-March) for the annual festival and Theyyam; Amavasi days for pitru tarpanam.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily per a business listing (verify - confirm locally).
